name: Hypomyelination with hypodontia and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (4H spectrum)

clinicalPearls: The clinically defined 4H phenotype is the triad of Hypomyelination, Hypodontia and Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, sitting within the POLR3-related leukodystrophy spectrum (POLR3A, POLR3B, POLR1C)
It is recognised as a distinctive syndromic presentation in which dental and endocrine clues point to a specific hypomyelinating leukodystrophy rather than an isolated white matter disorder
Neurological features are dominated by cerebellar signs, ataxia, intention tremor and a tremor-ataxia picture, often with spasticity, myopia and abnormal eye movements
Dental abnormalities include delayed dentition, hypodontia or oligodontia, an abnormal tooth eruption sequence and occasionally natal teeth
Endocrine involvement produces delayed, arrested or absent puberty from hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and may require hormone assessment and replacement

The MRI pattern is diffuse hypomyelination with cerebellar atrophy and relative T2 hypointensity of structures such as the optic radiations, anterolateral thalamus, globus pallidus, dentate nucleus and the corticospinal tracts in the posterior limb of the internal capsule
Diagnosis integrates MRI pattern recognition with the dental and endocrine triad, confirmed by POLR3-subunit gene testing; care is supportive with endocrine, dental and rehabilitation input
reference.pathophysiology: The 4H phenotype reflects deficient RNA polymerase III activity due to biallelic variants in genes encoding its subunits, most often POLR3A or POLR3B and sometimes POLR1C. RNA polymerase III transcribes small non-coding RNAs, including transfer RNAs and 5S ribosomal RNA, that are required for protein synthesis. Reduced output of these RNAs particularly affects tissues with high biosynthetic demand, so oligodendrocytes fail to produce adequate myelin (hypomyelination), tooth development is disturbed (hypodontia and abnormal eruption) and the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis functions poorly (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism). The convergence of these tissue effects generates the characteristic clinical triad.
additionalDifferentials: Other POLR3-related leukodystrophy presentations without the full triad
Kallmann syndrome and other causes of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with neurological features
Ectodermal dysplasias presenting with hypodontia and neurological signs
additionalInvestigations: Brain MRI to identify hypomyelination with cerebellar atrophy and the selectively preserved T2-hypointense structures
POLR3A, POLR3B and POLR1C sequencing, with panel or exome analysis if targeted testing is negative
Dental review and orthopantomogram to document hypodontia and abnormal dentition
Endocrine assessment of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis and pubertal staging
Ophthalmology review for myopia and eye-movement abnormalities
Bone health and growth monitoring in the context of hypogonadism
redFlags: Absent pubertal development requiring endocrine evaluation and treatment
Unexpectedly rapid neurological decline prompting reassessment
Recurrent falls from worsening ataxia and spasticity
reference.prognosis: The 4H phenotype is generally slowly progressive; children often gain skills before plateauing and then gradually declining, with cerebellar, motor and speech function increasingly affected. Severity ranges from mild adolescent-onset disease to more significant early-onset forms, and prognosis depends on the degree of motor and bulbar involvement as well as attention to endocrine and dental care.
pitfalls: Focusing on the white matter change and missing the diagnostic dental and endocrine clues of the triad
Not recognising the specific pattern of preserved T2-hypointense structures on MRI
Failing to identify and treat hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, affecting puberty and bone health
Assuming a static leukoencephalopathy and not pursuing POLR3 genetics
Omitting autosomal recessive genetic counselling for the family
references: Bradley and Daroff's Neurology in Clinical Practice
management: Manage the hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with hormone replacement to induce and maintain puberty and support bone health, guided by endocrinology
Provide comprehensive dental care for the hypodontia and abnormal eruption, with prosthetics and orthodontic or implant planning
Offer symptomatic treatment of cerebellar features, spasticity and tremor with physiotherapy and appropriate medication
Support motor, speech and cognitive function through multidisciplinary neurorehabilitation
Monitor and protect bone mineral density in the context of hypogonadism
Correct myopia and manage eye-movement abnormalities with ophthalmology input
Offer genetic counselling for this autosomal recessive POLR3-related disorder and test at-risk relatives
Monitor for progressive neurological decline and adjust supportive care accordingly
